part1_structural_finding.finding: T_k is defined on level k's own (p,q,r) space alone (dimension 2*(k+1)^2, different for each k). Z_i acts as literal identity on (p,q) by construction, so it cannot, even in principle, map a state's (p,q) content into a different level's (p,q) range. This holds for l_{e_i} too (Meier's own construction: a (k+1)-dim matrix acting entirely within level k's own p-index). Both are infinitesimal generators of the group's own left/right regular representation; Peter-Weyl levels are the isotypic components of that same representation, invariant under left and right translation by definition -- so any operator built purely from these generators is necessarily block-diagonal across levels, structurally, not as a limitation of a specific postulate.
